title: JAPAN'S ANUBIS
subtitle: the white foxes of Inari
source: Inari Okami and kitsune messengers; Inari shrine fox statues (key, jewel, red yodarekake); Fushimi Inari-taisha senbon torii (~10,000); aburaage, kitsune udon, inarizushi; folk belief of a tail per century

lines.say: [curious] Kon, Egypt has Anubis. Does Japan have one?
Meet Inari, the god of rice. Her messengers are white foxes.
Egypt's jackal is black, like the fertile soil of the Nile. Japan's fox is white... and it guards the rice.
cap: like the fertile soil of the Nile.

lines.say: Inari has over thirty thousand shrines. And at almost every one, two stone foxes stand guard.
One holds a key to the rice storehouse. The other holds a jewel.
People dress them in red bibs, and leave them fried tofu. It's their favorite.
[amused] That's why inari sushi is called inari.
[delighted] Okay, I'm eating ALL the inari sushi.
At Fushimi Inari in Kyoto, ten thousand red gates tunnel up the mountain. Some say the foxes walk them at night.
[sly] Every one of those gates was donated by a business, and the company's name is carved right into the wood.
[hushed] And legend says the oldest foxes grow a new tail every hundred years... until they have nine.
cap: And legend says the oldest foxes

lines.say: [suspicious] Wait. Red bib... white fur... Kon, are YOU one of them?
